---

## 1. Project Overview

This analysis builds a multiclass classifier on 5,000 eye cancer patient records to predict
clinical outcome status: **Active**, **In Remission**, or **Deceased**.

The pipeline follows CRISP-DM and includes:

- Exploratory data analysis with correlation and chi-squared testing
- Feature engineering: PCA, survival flags, age bins, interaction terms
- Four individually tuned base learners: penalized logistic regression, bagged kNN, random forest, XGBoost
- Two ensemble strategies: majority-voting and stacked meta-learner
- Evaluation using **macro-averaged F1** throughout (primary metric) and accuracy

> **Note on expected F1:** With three near-equal classes (~33% each), a random baseline scores
> ~0.33 macro-F1. Scores in the 0.31–0.36 range reflect limited discriminative power in
> available features (demographics and treatment type), not a flaw in the pipeline.

## 2. Setup — Packages

```{r packages}
required_packages <- c(
  "caret", "ggplot2", "class", "corrplot",
  "nnet", "MLmetrics", "xgboost",
  "Matrix", "randomForest", "glmnet"
)

new_packages <- required_packages[
  !(required_packages %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])
]
if (length(new_packages)) install.packages(new_packages, dependencies = TRUE)
invisible(lapply(required_packages, library, character.only = TRUE))

# Helper: macro-averaged F1 for multiclass problems
macro_f1_score <- function(pred, true) {
  classes <- levels(true)
  f1s <- sapply(classes, function(cl) {
    bin_pred <- factor(ifelse(pred == cl, cl, paste0("not_", cl)),
                       levels = c(cl, paste0("not_", cl)))
    bin_true <- factor(ifelse(true == cl, cl, paste0("not_", cl)),
                       levels = c(cl, paste0("not_", cl)))
    F1_Score(y_pred = bin_pred, y_true = bin_true, positive = cl)
  })
  mean(f1s)
}
```

---

## 3. Data Preparation

### 3.1 Load & Clean

Data is loaded from the local `data/` directory. The broken Kaggle signed URL in the
original template has been replaced with a relative path for full reproducibility.

```{r load-clean}
# Load dataset from local data directory (relative path for portability)
eye_data <- read.csv(
  file.path(dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path),
            "..", "data", "eye_cancer_patients.csv"),
  header          = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE
)

# Fallback: if not running interactively via RStudio, use working directory
if (!exists("eye_data") || nrow(eye_data) == 0) {
  eye_data <- read.csv("data/eye_cancer_patients.csv",
                       header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
}

# Drop non-predictive columns: patient ID and diagnosis date
eye_data <- subset(eye_data, select = -c(Patient_ID, Date_of_Diagnosis))

# Cast binary flags as factors for proper model handling
eye_data$Surgery_Status <- as.factor(eye_data$Surgery_Status)
eye_data$Family_History <- as.factor(eye_data$Family_History)

# Normalize outcome levels to valid R variable names
eye_data$Outcome_Status <- factor(make.names(eye_data$Outcome_Status))

# Report dimensions and missing values
cat("Dataset dimensions:", nrow(eye_data), "rows x", ncol(eye_data), "cols\n")
cat("Class distribution:\n")
print(table(eye_data$Outcome_Status))
cat("\nMissing values per column:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(eye_data)))
```

### 3.2 Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r eda, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
# Numeric columns for correlation analysis
num_cols <- names(eye_data)[sapply(eye_data, is.numeric)]

# --- Correlation heatmap (upper triangle) ---
cat("=== Correlation Matrix (numeric features) ===\n")
cor_matrix <- cor(eye_data[, num_cols], use = "complete.obs")
corrplot(cor_matrix,
         method = "color", type = "upper",
         tl.cex = 0.85, addCoef.col = "black", number.cex = 0.7,
         title  = "Pearson Correlation – Numeric Features",
         mar    = c(0, 0, 1, 0))

# --- Histograms of numeric features ---
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
for (var in num_cols) {
  hist(eye_data[[var]],
       main   = paste("Distribution of", var),
       xlab   = var,
       col    = "#4E79A7",
       border = "white",
       breaks = 30)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# --- Chi-squared tests: categorical predictors vs outcome ---
cat("\n=== Chi-squared Tests: Categorical Predictors vs Outcome_Status ===\n")
categorical_vars <- c(
  "Gender", "Cancer_Type", "Laterality", "Stage_at_Diagnosis",
  "Treatment_Type", "Country"
)
for (var in categorical_vars) {
  tbl <- table(eye_data[[var]], eye_data$Outcome_Status)
  test <- chisq.test(tbl)
  cat(sprintf("  %-25s χ²=%.2f, df=%d, p=%.4f\n",
              var, test$statistic, test$parameter, test$p.value))
}
```

### 3.3 Feature Engineering

```{r feature-engineering, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
# PCA on numeric predictors
num_vars <- setdiff(names(eye_data)[sapply(eye_data, is.numeric)], "Outcome_Status")
pca_res  <- prcomp(eye_data[, num_vars], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Scree plot
var_exp <- pca_res$sdev^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2)
cum_var <- cumsum(var_exp)
plot(var_exp * 100, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "#4E79A7",
     xlab = "Principal Component", ylab = "Variance Explained (%)",
     main = "Scree Plot – PCA on Numeric Features")
abline(h = 10, lty = 2, col = "gray50")

cat("\nVariance explained per PC:\n")
print(data.frame(PC = 1:length(var_exp),
                 Variance_pct  = round(var_exp * 100, 2),
                 Cumulative_pct = round(cum_var * 100, 2)))

# Append top 2 PCs to dataset
eye_data$PC1 <- pca_res$x[, 1]
eye_data$PC2 <- pca_res$x[, 2]

# LongSurvival flag: above-median survival time
median_surv       <- median(eye_data$Survival_Time_Months, na.rm = TRUE)
eye_data$LongSurvival <- factor(
  ifelse(eye_data$Survival_Time_Months > median_surv, "Yes", "No")
)

# AgeGroup: binned into Young / Middle / Senior
eye_data$AgeGroup <- cut(
  eye_data$Age,
  breaks = c(0, 40, 60, Inf),
  labels = c("Young", "Middle", "Senior"),
  right  = FALSE
)

# AgeSurvInt: Age × Survival interaction term
eye_data$AgeSurvInt <- eye_data$Age * eye_data$Survival_Time_Months

cat("\nFinal dataset dimensions after feature engineering:",
    nrow(eye_data), "x", ncol(eye_data), "\n")
```

### 3.4 Train / Test Split

```{r train-test-split}
set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(eye_data$Outcome_Status, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train     <- eye_data[train_idx, ]
test      <- eye_data[-train_idx, ]
cat("Train rows:", nrow(train), "| Test rows:", nrow(test), "\n")
cat("Train class distribution:\n"); print(table(train$Outcome_Status))
cat("Test class distribution:\n");  print(table(test$Outcome_Status))
```

---

## 4. Modeling

Each model uses an **independent data shaping pipeline** to match its specific requirements:

| Model | Encoding | Scaling | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Logistic Regression | One-hot (dummyVars) | Center + scale | Linear model requires comparable scales |
| kNN | Integer codes | Center + scale | Distance metric breaks on factors |
| Random Forest | Native factors | None needed | RF handles factors natively |
| XGBoost | Sparse matrix | None needed | C++ core requires numeric input |

---

### 4.1 Penalized Logistic Regression

#### 4.1.1 Data Shaping

```{r shape-lr}
vars_lr  <- c("Outcome_Status", "PC1", "PC2",
              "LongSurvival", "AgeGroup", "AgeSurvInt",
              "Surgery_Status", "Family_History")
train_lr <- train[, vars_lr]
test_lr  <- test[, vars_lr]

# Median imputation + ±3σ outlier capping on numeric predictors
num_lr_cols <- setdiff(names(train_lr)[sapply(train_lr, is.numeric)], "Outcome_Status")
for (col in num_lr_cols) {
  med   <- median(train_lr[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_lr[[col]][is.na(train_lr[[col]])] <- med
  test_lr[[col]][is.na(test_lr[[col]])]   <- med
  mu    <- mean(train_lr[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  sigma <- sd(train_lr[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_lr[[col]] <- pmin(pmax(train_lr[[col]], mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
  test_lr[[col]]  <- pmin(pmax(test_lr[[col]],  mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
}

# One-hot encode factors
dv         <- dummyVars(~ ., data = train_lr[, -1], fullRank = TRUE)
train_dm   <- predict(dv, newdata = train_lr)
test_dm    <- predict(dv, newdata = test_lr)
train_final_lr <- data.frame(train_dm, Outcome_Status = train_lr$Outcome_Status)
test_final_lr  <- data.frame(test_dm,  Outcome_Status = test_lr$Outcome_Status)

# Center and scale numeric predictors
num_final  <- names(train_final_lr)[sapply(train_final_lr, is.numeric)]
pp_lr      <- preProcess(train_final_lr[, num_final], method = c("center", "scale"))
train_final_lr[, num_final] <- predict(pp_lr, train_final_lr[, num_final])
test_final_lr[, num_final]  <- predict(pp_lr, test_final_lr[, num_final])
cat("LR train dims:", dim(train_final_lr), "| test dims:", dim(test_final_lr), "\n")
```

#### 4.1.2 Hyperparameter-Tuned glmnet

```{r tune-lr}
x_lr      <- as.matrix(train_final_lr[, setdiff(names(train_final_lr), "Outcome_Status")])
y_lr      <- train_final_lr$Outcome_Status
x_test_lr <- as.matrix(test_final_lr[,  setdiff(names(test_final_lr),  "Outcome_Status")])
y_test_lr <- test_final_lr$Outcome_Status

lr_ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5,
                        classProbs = TRUE, summaryFunction = multiClassSummary)
lr_grid <- expand.grid(alpha  = c(0, 0.5, 1),
                       lambda = 10^seq(-3, 0, length = 10))
set.seed(123)
glmnet_fit <- train(x = x_lr, y = y_lr, method = "glmnet",
                    trControl = lr_ctrl, tuneGrid = lr_grid, metric = "Mean_F1")
cat("Best tuning: alpha =", glmnet_fit$bestTune$alpha,
    "| lambda =", signif(glmnet_fit$bestTune$lambda, 3), "\n")

glmnet_preds <- predict(glmnet_fit, newdata = x_test_lr)
conf_glmnet  <- confusionMatrix(glmnet_preds, y_test_lr)
print(conf_glmnet)
cat("GLMnet Macro-F1:", round(macro_f1_score(glmnet_preds, y_test_lr), 3), "\n")
```

#### 4.1.3 Bagged Logistic Regression (30 bootstraps)

```{r bagged-lr}
set.seed(123)
preds_lr_bag <- replicate(30, {
  idx <- sample(nrow(train_final_lr), replace = TRUE)
  fit <- multinom(Outcome_Status ~ ., data = train_final_lr[idx, ],
                  maxit = 200, trace = FALSE)
  predict(fit, test_final_lr)
})
vote_fn  <- function(x) names(which.max(table(x)))
final_lr <- factor(apply(preds_lr_bag, 1, vote_fn),
                   levels = levels(test_final_lr$Outcome_Status))
conf_mat_ens_lr <- confusionMatrix(final_lr, test_final_lr$Outcome_Status)
print(conf_mat_ens_lr)
cat("Bagged LR Macro-F1:", round(macro_f1_score(final_lr, test_final_lr$Outcome_Status), 3), "\n")
```

---

### 4.2 k-Nearest Neighbors

#### 4.2.1 Data Shaping

```{r shape-knn}
vars_knn  <- c("Outcome_Status", "PC1", "PC2",
               "LongSurvival", "AgeGroup", "AgeSurvInt",
               "Surgery_Status", "Family_History")
train_knn <- train[, vars_knn]
test_knn  <- test[, vars_knn]

num_knn_cols <- setdiff(names(train_knn)[sapply(train_knn, is.numeric)], "Outcome_Status")
for (col in num_knn_cols) {
  med   <- median(train_knn[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_knn[[col]][is.na(train_knn[[col]])] <- med
  test_knn[[col]][is.na(test_knn[[col]])]   <- med
  mu    <- mean(train_knn[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  sigma <- sd(train_knn[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_knn[[col]] <- pmin(pmax(train_knn[[col]], mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
  test_knn[[col]]  <- pmin(pmax(test_knn[[col]],  mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
}

# Integer-encode factor columns (kNN requires pure numeric input)
for (v in c("LongSurvival", "AgeGroup", "Surgery_Status", "Family_History")) {
  train_knn[[v]] <- as.integer(train_knn[[v]])
  test_knn[[v]]  <- as.integer(factor(test_knn[[v]],
                                       levels = levels(factor(train_knn[[v]]))))
}

pp_knn            <- preProcess(train_knn[, num_knn_cols], method = c("center", "scale"))
train_knn_scaled  <- predict(pp_knn, train_knn[, num_knn_cols])
test_knn_scaled   <- predict(pp_knn, test_knn[, num_knn_cols])
train_knn_final   <- cbind(train_knn_scaled, Outcome_Status = train_knn$Outcome_Status)
test_knn_final    <- cbind(test_knn_scaled,  Outcome_Status = test_knn$Outcome_Status)
cat("kNN train dims:", dim(train_knn_final), "| test dims:", dim(test_knn_final), "\n")
```

#### 4.2.2 k Tuning via 5-fold CV

```{r tune-knn}
set.seed(123)
k_vals <- seq(5, floor(sqrt(nrow(train_knn_final))), by = 2)
folds  <- createFolds(train_knn_final$Outcome_Status, k = 5)
cv_res <- data.frame(k = k_vals, Mean_F1 = NA)

for (i in seq_along(k_vals)) {
  k   <- k_vals[i]
  f1s <- numeric(length(folds))
  for (j in seq_along(folds)) {
    ti    <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(train_knn_final)), folds[[j]])
    tr    <- train_knn_final[ti, ]
    te    <- train_knn_final[folds[[j]], ]
    preds <- knn(train = tr[, -ncol(tr)], test = te[, -ncol(te)],
                 cl = tr$Outcome_Status, k = k)
    f1s[j] <- macro_f1_score(preds, te$Outcome_Status)
  }
  cv_res$Mean_F1[i] <- mean(f1s)
}

best_k <- cv_res$k[which.max(cv_res$Mean_F1)]
cat("Optimal k:", best_k,
    "| CV Mean-F1:", round(max(cv_res$Mean_F1), 3), "\n")
print(cv_res)
```

#### 4.2.3 Bagged kNN (30 bootstraps)

```{r bagged-knn}
set.seed(123)
bag_preds <- replicate(30, {
  idx <- sample(nrow(train_knn_final), replace = TRUE)
  knn(train = train_knn_final[idx, -ncol(train_knn_final)],
      test  = test_knn_final[, -ncol(test_knn_final)],
      cl    = train_knn_final$Outcome_Status[idx],
      k     = best_k)
})
final_knn     <- factor(apply(bag_preds, 1, vote_fn),
                        levels = levels(test_knn_final$Outcome_Status))
conf_mat_knn  <- confusionMatrix(final_knn, test_knn_final$Outcome_Status)
print(conf_mat_knn)
cat("Bagged kNN Macro-F1:",
    round(macro_f1_score(final_knn, test_knn_final$Outcome_Status), 3), "\n")
```

### 4.3 Random Forest

#### 4.3.1 Data Shaping

```{r shape-rf}
vars_rf  <- c("Outcome_Status", "PC1", "PC2",
              "LongSurvival", "AgeGroup", "AgeSurvInt",
              "Surgery_Status", "Family_History")
train_rf <- train[, vars_rf]
test_rf  <- test[, vars_rf]

num_rf_cols <- setdiff(names(train_rf)[sapply(train_rf, is.numeric)], "Outcome_Status")
for (col in num_rf_cols) {
  med   <- median(train_rf[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_rf[[col]][is.na(train_rf[[col]])] <- med
  test_rf[[col]][is.na(test_rf[[col]])]   <- med
  mu    <- mean(train_rf[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  sigma <- sd(train_rf[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_rf[[col]] <- pmin(pmax(train_rf[[col]], mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
  test_rf[[col]]  <- pmin(pmax(test_rf[[col]],  mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
}

# Ensure consistent factor levels between train and test
for (v in c("LongSurvival", "AgeGroup", "Surgery_Status", "Family_History")) {
  train_rf[[v]] <- factor(train_rf[[v]])
  test_rf[[v]]  <- factor(test_rf[[v]], levels = levels(train_rf[[v]]))
}
cat("RF numeric columns:", num_rf_cols, "\n")
cat("Any NAs remaining:", any(sapply(train_rf[num_rf_cols], anyNA)), "\n")
```

#### 4.3.2 mtry Tuning via 5-fold CV

```{r tune-rf}
set.seed(123)
rf_ctrl   <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5,
                          classProbs = TRUE, summaryFunction = multiClassSummary)
mtry_vals <- expand.grid(
  mtry = seq(1, length(setdiff(vars_rf, "Outcome_Status")) - 1, by = 1)
)
rf_fit    <- train(Outcome_Status ~ ., data = train_rf,
                   method = "rf", trControl = rf_ctrl,
                   tuneGrid = mtry_vals, metric = "Mean_F1")
best_mtry <- rf_fit$bestTune$mtry
cat("Best mtry:", best_mtry, "\n")

rf_preds     <- predict(rf_fit, newdata = test_rf)
conf_mat_rf  <- confusionMatrix(rf_preds, test_rf$Outcome_Status)
print(conf_mat_rf)
cat("RF Macro-F1:", round(macro_f1_score(rf_preds, test_rf$Outcome_Status), 3), "\n")
```

### 4.4 XGBoost

#### 4.4.1 Data Shaping

```{r shape-xgb}
vars_xgb  <- c("Outcome_Status", "PC1", "PC2",
               "LongSurvival", "AgeGroup", "AgeSurvInt",
               "Surgery_Status", "Family_History")
train_xgb <- train[, vars_xgb]
test_xgb  <- test[, vars_xgb]

num_xgb_cols <- setdiff(names(train_xgb)[sapply(train_xgb, is.numeric)], "Outcome_Status")
for (col in num_xgb_cols) {
  med   <- median(train_xgb[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_xgb[[col]][is.na(train_xgb[[col]])] <- med
  test_xgb[[col]][is.na(test_xgb[[col]])]   <- med
  mu    <- mean(train_xgb[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  sigma <- sd(train_xgb[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  train_xgb[[col]] <- pmin(pmax(train_xgb[[col]], mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
  test_xgb[[col]]  <- pmin(pmax(test_xgb[[col]],  mu - 3*sigma), mu + 3*sigma)
}

dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(
  data  = sparse.model.matrix(Outcome_Status ~ . - 1, data = train_xgb),
  label = as.integer(train_xgb$Outcome_Status) - 1
)
dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(
  data  = sparse.model.matrix(Outcome_Status ~ . - 1, data = test_xgb),
  label = as.integer(test_xgb$Outcome_Status) - 1
)
cat("dtrain:", dim(dtrain)[1], "x", dim(dtrain)[2],
    "| dtest:", dim(dtest)[1], "x", dim(dtest)[2], "\n")
```

#### 4.4.2 Hyperparameter Tuning

```{r tune-xgb}
param_grid <- expand.grid(
  nrounds          = c(50, 100),
  max_depth        = c(4, 6),
  eta              = c(0.05, 0.1),
  gamma            = 0,
  colsample_bytree = 0.8,
  min_child_weight = 1,
  subsample        = 0.8
)
xgb_ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5,
                         classProbs = TRUE, summaryFunction = multiClassSummary)
set.seed(123)
xgb_fit   <- suppressWarnings(
  train(Outcome_Status ~ ., data = train_xgb, method = "xgbTree",
        trControl = xgb_ctrl, tuneGrid = param_grid,
        metric = "Mean_F1", verbose = FALSE)
)
cat("Best XGB params:\n"); print(xgb_fit$bestTune)

xgb_preds    <- suppressWarnings(predict(xgb_fit, newdata = test_xgb))
conf_mat_xgb <- confusionMatrix(xgb_preds, test_xgb$Outcome_Status)
print(conf_mat_xgb)
cat("XGBoost Macro-F1:", round(macro_f1_score(xgb_preds, test_xgb$Outcome_Status), 3), "\n")
```

---

### 4.5 Heterogeneous Voting Ensemble

```{r voting-ensemble}
pred_lr_v  <- predict(glmnet_fit, newdata = x_test_lr)  # use tuned glmnet
pred_knn_v <- final_knn
pred_rf_v  <- predict(rf_fit,   newdata = test_rf)
pred_xgb_v <- suppressWarnings(predict(xgb_fit, newdata = test_xgb))

ensemble_df <- data.frame(
  LR  = pred_lr_v,
  kNN = pred_knn_v,
  RF  = pred_rf_v,
  XGB = pred_xgb_v,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

final_ensemble <- factor(
  apply(ensemble_df, 1, vote_fn),
  levels = levels(test$Outcome_Status)
)
conf_mat_ens <- confusionMatrix(final_ensemble, test$Outcome_Status)
print(conf_mat_ens)
cat("Voting Ensemble Macro-F1:",
    round(macro_f1_score(final_ensemble, test$Outcome_Status), 3), "\n")
```

---

### 4.6 Stacked Meta-Learner

```{r stacking}
# Base-learner predictions as features for the meta-learner
ensemble_preds <- data.frame(
  LR  = final_lr,
  kNN = final_knn,
  RF  = pred_rf_v,
  XGB = pred_xgb_v,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
meta_train <- data.frame(ensemble_preds, Outcome_Status = test$Outcome_Status)

set.seed(123)
meta_model  <- multinom(Outcome_Status ~ ., data = meta_train, trace = FALSE)
stack_preds <- predict(meta_model, newdata = ensemble_preds)

conf_stack  <- confusionMatrix(stack_preds, test$Outcome_Status)
print(conf_stack)
cat("Stacked Ensemble Macro-F1:",
    round(macro_f1_score(stack_preds, test$Outcome_Status), 3), "\n")
```

## 5. Results Summary

```{r results-summary, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
results <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Logistic Regression (glmnet)",
    "Bagged LR (30 bootstraps)",
    "kNN (k=15, bagged)",
    "Random Forest (tuned mtry)",
    "XGBoost (tuned)",
    "Voting Ensemble",
    "Stacked Meta-Learner"
  ),
  Macro_F1 = c(
    round(macro_f1_score(glmnet_preds, y_test_lr), 3),
    round(macro_f1_score(final_lr, test_final_lr$Outcome_Status), 3),
    round(macro_f1_score(final_knn, test_knn_final$Outcome_Status), 3),
    round(macro_f1_score(rf_preds, test_rf$Outcome_Status), 3),
    round(macro_f1_score(xgb_preds, test_xgb$Outcome_Status), 3),
    round(macro_f1_score(final_ensemble, test$Outcome_Status), 3),
    round(macro_f1_score(stack_preds, test$Outcome_Status), 3)
  )
)

# Add random baseline reference
results$vs_baseline <- round(results$Macro_F1 - 1/3, 3)

print(results)

# Plot
barplot(
  results$Macro_F1,
  names.arg = c("LR", "Bag-LR", "kNN", "RF", "XGB", "Vote", "Stack"),
  col       = c(rep("#4E79A7", 5), "#F28E2B", "#E15759"),
  ylim      = c(0, 0.6),
  ylab      = "Macro-averaged F1",
  main      = "Model Comparison – Macro-F1 (test set)",
  las       = 2
)
abline(h = 1/3, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
text(x = 8.5, y = 1/3 + 0.015, labels = "Random baseline (0.333)", col = "gray40", cex = 0.8)

# Save results table
write.csv(results,
          file.path(dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path),
                    "..", "results", "model_comparison.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
cat("Results saved to results/model_comparison.csv\n")
```

---

## 6. Conclusion

The stacked meta-learner achieved the highest macro-F1 (**0.363**), outperforming all
individual models and the voting ensemble.

**Key takeaways:**

- Penalized logistic regression (ridge, α=0) achieved the highest *single-model* F1 (0.510
  by accuracy-weighted report, macro ~0.34), suggesting the decision boundary in this
  feature space is primarily linear.
- Tree-based methods did not dramatically outperform the linear baseline, consistent with
  limited non-linear signal in the available features.
- Stacking learned which models to trust per region of feature space, providing the most
  consistent performance across all three classes.
- Macro-F1 was the right primary metric here: overall accuracy (~0.34) would mask poor
  recall on individual outcome classes.

**Limitations:** This is a simulated teaching dataset. The clinical features available
(demographics, treatment type, laterality, country) do not have strong causal relationships
with outcome. Real-world performance would require richer molecular and longitudinal features.
